audit_items.proof_trace: next_fork_version uses next_fork_epoch() which returns the next named fork (ForkName), while next_fork_epoch field uses next_digest_epoch() which includes BPO epochs from blob_schedule. For BPO forks, next_fork_version incorrectly advances to the next named fork version instead of remaining at current_fork_version.
audit_items.attack_scenario: During a BPO fork (blob parameter change), peers advertise next_fork_version pointing to a future named fork instead of current version. This breaks peer discovery as nodes filter by fork_digest match but expect next_fork_version to remain stable across BPO forks, causing network fragmentation.
